79738206.title: Trichy assault rifle
79738206.extract:
The Trichy assault rifle (TAR), sometimes known as the Tiruchi assault rifle, is an Indian-made assault rifle chambered for the 7.62×39mm round. The TAR is based on the AR-M1, produced by Bulgarian manufacturer Arsenal AD. Developed between 2011 and 2015, Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli (OFT) began manufacturing TARs in 2017.
The TAR was developed to reduce dependence on imported AR-M1s under the Atmanirbhar Bharat self-reliance policy. The TAR has been adopted by most Indian law enforcement agencies.


== History ==


=== Background ===
Prior to the TAR's introduction, India largely used foreign-made AK-style rifles. Around 500,000 M1s were reportedly imported by India from Bulgaria in 2021 for use by the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) and Indian police forces. As of May 2025, India is the second-largest arms importer after Ukraine, accounting for 8.3% of the arms trade, according to research data from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. To reduce dependence on importing small arms from other countries, part of the Atmanirbhar Bharat policy called for self-sufficiency to manufacture firearms in India. 
OFT announced the manufacture of an indigenous AK-based assault rifle in 2011. The AR was named Trichy after OFT to recognise the factory's contribution in developing and manufacturing the rifle. Some TARs were made in 2012 to be tested. These early TARs were tested by the Border Security Force (BSF), the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), the Indo-Tibetan Border Police and the Sashastra Seema Bal.
Development started in 2015 with a production line established in 2017. That March, 200 TARs were acquired by the Chhattisgarh Police as part of the 216th Ordnance Factories Day celebration. Concerns were raised at the time, prior to manufacture, that OFT was experiencing manpower decline, leading to a decline of employees at the company. The All India Defence Employees Federation, the Indian National Defence Workers' Federation, and the Bharatiya Pratiraksha Mazdoor Sangh stated their opposition to importing small arms with the unions hoping that more orders for the TAR would be approved, retaining employees at OFT.


=== Adoption ===

In November 2017, the CRPF conducted field tests to determine the suitability of the TAR with 15,000 rounds fired at the CRPF Academy in Kadarpur, Haryana with no reports of the rifle jamming. Other tests conducted included the TAR being fired from mud, rain and saltwater and from being dropped to test reliability and accuracy. 100 TARs were ordered afterwards. In February 2018, further tests were conducted by the CRPF at Jagdalpur, Raipur, Guwahati and Srinagar with an order of 6,167 TARs placed afterwards. At the time, the CRPF tested the Trichy with the Ghatak, the Joint Venture Protective Carbine and the INSAS1C. In March 2020, the CRPF acquired the first 500 out of 6,167 TARs sold to them.
In January 2019, the TAR was delivered to the BSF, with its Additional Director General Nasir Kamal receiving the first rifle from the Ordnance Factory Board's Director General Saurabh Kumar. It was reported in the same month that the Jharkhand Police would acquire TARs for anti-Naxalite operations. The TAR was displayed for the first time at the Pragati Maidan in New Delhi for the 5th International Police Expo and the 4th India Homeland Security Expo. In February 2020, the TAR was on public display at the Defence Expo at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. It was reported at the time that the TAR was offered to the Indian Army. OFT reported in March 2021 that around 11,500 TARs were supplied for a total of Rs 1.60 billion during fiscal year 2020–21.
In January 2021, the TriCa (Trichy Carbine) Carbine was unveiled. Tests were conducted where 2,000 rounds were fired with no stoppages. That August, OFT announced that the TAR could use the ARDE Under Barrel Grenade Launcher, which was presented by OFT general manager Sanjay Dwivedi. A TAR variant with a downfolding stock was presented publicly. This variant was sought out by the Railway Protection Force aside from the CAPFs. In December 2021, the National Security Guard placed an order of 100 TriCa carbines. On April 2022, the Kerala Police (KP) ordered 92 TriCa carbines. According to OFT, the Greyhounds unit ordered 44 TARs. In July 2022, the Government of Kerala received a request from KP to procure 250 TARs with side folding stocks; they received the TriCa carbines in May 2025. According to the Advanced Weapons and Equipment India's (AWEIL) 2022–2023 Annual Report, the National Security Guard and the Andhra Pradesh Police conducted tests on both the TAR and the TriCa carbine. 
In January 2023, the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) received TARs manufactured from Rifle Factory Ishapore. That April, Minister of State for Defence and Tourism Ajay Bhatt visited OFT, where he witnessed the TAR being manufactured in the factory while briefed on OFT's research and development work. The following January, BSF procured further TARs featuring bayonets. The Government of Kerala published an approved plan for the KP to acquire 30 TARs. In November 2023, the Trichy was on display at the Dasara Exhibition in Mysore, Karnataka as part of an effort to raise awareness on crime and public safety. In a July 2024 interview with Rajesh Choudhary, Chairman and Managing Director of AWEIL, he said that the TAR continues to be in demand with CAPFs and reported that an export order was made for the rifle. In May 2025, it was reported that the Assam Forest Department and the Central Bureau of Narcotics made orders for the TriCa carbine.


=== Development ===
Initial versions of the TAR were produced by using FN FAL-based receivers and were using 7.62x39 mm magazines. In 2012, there were reports that the prototypes jammed during testing due to the rate of fire being 800 rounds per minutes instead of 600 rounds per minute to match with the AK-47. It was initially expected that the rate of fire would be at 650 rounds per minute. 
The current version of the TAR is based on the AR-M1 with a machined receiver instead of stamped sheet to ensure the rifle has high accuracy and reliability. The TAR can be outfitted with picatinny rails on the upper handguard to attach scopes if requested.


=== Combat use ===
In July 2021, it was reported that the TARs used by the Kerala Police are effective in Naxalite-Maoist counterinsurgency operations.
On August 2025, a TAR was secured from pro-Maoist communist Naxalite fighters in Chhattisgarh’s Narayanpur district.


== Design ==
The TAR can fire with single, burst and full automatic mode. OFT reported that the TAR can be adopted with single shot mode only for police forces in cities and urban areas. While it has an effective range of 300 to 350 metres, the range can be up to 500 metres if the rifle is used in full auto. 
OFT claimed that the TAR is functionally on par with the AK-47. 


=== Accessories ===
The TAR can be equipped with several underbarrel grenade launchers, including the ARDE UBGL, the GP-25, the GP-30 and the Arsenal M6 UBGL. The TAR can use bayonets.


=== Magazines ===
Magazines for the TAR are supplied by Nilkamal Limited. Magazines made for AK-47-based assault rifles can also be used.


=== Ammunition ===
7.62×39 mm ammunition of all types can be used for the TAR.


== Variants ==


=== Trichy assault rifle ===
Main variant with a fixed stock.


=== Trichy folding stock (side) ===
TAR variant with a side folding stock.


=== Trichy folding stock (down) ===
Unveiled on August 2021, it is a TAR variant with a downfolding stock. 
It's sometimes referred to as a variant with an underfolding stock.


=== Trichy Carbine (TriCa) ===
Unveiled on January 2021, the TriCa weights 3.17 kg and is marketed as a compact weapon for vehicle crews, paratroopers and special forces units. The TriCA's firing range is from 150-175 metres. A muzzle device is installed on the barrel to minimize muzzle flash and sound when it's fired.
The TriCa is a clone based on the Arsenal AR-M14SF, but the muzzle device is based on the AKS-74U.
It is sometimes known as Baby TAR or TAR-3.


== Users ==
 India:
Border Security Force
Central Industrial Security Force
Central Reserve Police Force
Chhattisgarh Police
Greater Mumbai Police
Indo-Tibetan Border Police
Jharkhand Police
Kerala Police
Madhya Pradesh Police
National Security Guard
Rajasthan Police
Unnamed country: Rajesh Choudhary of AWEIL reported an export order from an unnamed country.


=== Non-state actors ===
People's Liberation Guerrilla Army (India): At least one Trichy recovered from Naxalite guerrillas.


== Notes ==


== References ==


== External links ==

approves Trichy Assault Rifle after tests|date=28 October 2017|accessdate=2025-04-16|archivedate=2017-10-30|author=Raman Krishnamoorthy|work=The Hindu }} The [[All India Defence Employees Federation]], the [[Indian National Defence Workers' Federation]], and the [[Bharatiya Pratiraksha Mazdoor Sangh]] stated their opposition to importing small arms with the unions hoping that more orders for the TAR would be approved, retaining employees at OFT.{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171030190450/https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Tiruchirapalli/crpf-approves-trichy-assault-rifle-after-tests/article19937479.ece|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Tiruchirapalli/crpf-approves-trichy-assault-rifle-after-tests/article19937479.ece|title=CRPF approves Trichy Assault Rifle after tests|date=28 October 2017|accessdate=2025-04-16|archivedate=2017-10-30|author=Raman Krishnamoorthy|work=The Hindu }} ===Adoption=== [[File:Firing TAR at range.jpg|thumb|right|A [[Central Industrial Security Force|CISF]] officer practices with the TAR at a shooting range.]] In November 2017, the CRPF conducted field tests to determine the suitability of the TAR with 15,000 rounds fired at the [[CRPF Academy]] in Kadarpur, [[Haryana]] with no reports of the rifle jamming.{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240624021152/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/trichy/crpf-gets-500-trichy-assault-rifles/articleshow/74595743.cms|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/trichy/crpf-gets-500-trichy-assault-rifles/articleshow/74595743.cms|title=CRPF gets 500 Trichy Assault Rifles|work=The Times of India|accessdate=2025-04-16|archivedate=2024-06-24|author=Deepak Karthik|date=12 March 2020 }} Other tests conducted included the TAR being fired from mud, rain and saltwater and from being dropped to test reliability and accuracy.{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250418024553/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/trichy/oft-hands-over-first-batch-of-500-trichy-assault-rifles-to-crpf/articleshow/74602309.cms|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/trichy/oft-hands-over-first-batch-of-500-trichy-assault-rifles-to-crpf/articleshow/74602309.cms|title=OFT hands over first batch of 500 Trichy Assault Rifles to CRPF|work=The Times of India|date=13 March 2020|author=Deepak Karthik|accessdate=2025-04-18|archivedate=2025-04-18}} 100 TARs were ordered afterwards. In February 2018, further tests were conducted by the CRPF at Jagdalpur, Raipur, Guwahati and Srinagar with an order of 6,167 TARs placed afterwards. At the time, the CRPF tested the Trichy with the Ghatak, the [[Joint Venture Protective Carbine]] and the [[INSAS rifle|INSAS]]1C.{{Cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180308202218/https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/crpf-to-conduct-trials-of-made-in-india-rifles-1174834-2018-02-21|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/crpf-to-conduct-trials-of-made-in-india-rifles-1174834-2018-02-21|title=CRPF to conduct trials of "Made in India" rifles|date=2018-02-21|publisher=India Today|accessdate=2025-10-30|archivedate=2018-03-08|author=Kamaljit Sandhu}} In March 2020, the CRPF acquired the first 500 out of 6,167 TARs sold to them. In January 2019, the TAR was delivered to the BSF, with its Additional Director General Nasir Kamal receiving the first rifle from the [[Directorate of Ordnance (Coordination & Services)|Ordnance Factory Board]]'s Director General Saurabh Kumar. It was reported in the same month that the [[Jharkhand Police]] would acquire TARs for anti-Naxalite operations.{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210425202943/https://www.telegraphindia.com/jharkhand/weapon-upgrade-for-jharkhand-police/cid/1682946|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/jharkhand/weapon-upgrade-for-jharkhand-police/cid/1682946|title=Weapon upgrade for state cops|date=27 January 2019|work=The Telegraph (India)|accessdate=2025-04-20|archivedate=2021-04-25|author=Vijay Deo Jha}} The TAR was displayed for the first time at the Pragati Maidan in [[New Delhi]] for the 5th International Police Expo and the 4th India Homeland Security Expo.{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015054750/https://www.internationalpoliceexpo.com/download/PER18.pdf|archive-date=2022-10-15|title=Post Event Report|accessdate=2022-10-15|url=https://www.internationalpoliceexpo.com/download/PER18.pdf|date=2019-07-01|publisher=International Police Expo}} In February 2020, the TAR was on public display at the Defence Expo at [[Lucknow]], [[Uttar Pradesh]].{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240714081440/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/nagpur/indian-assault-rifle-giving-stiff-competition-to-latest-russian-ak/articleshow/73941601.cms|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/nagpur/indian-assault-rifle-giving-stiff-competition-to-latest-russian-ak/articleshow/73941601.cms|title=Indian assault rifle giving stiff competition to latest Russian AK|date=5 February 2020|work=The Times of India|archivedate=2024-07-14|accessdate=2024-07-16|author=Shishir Arya}} It was reported at the time that the TAR was offered to the [[Indian Army]]. OFT reported in March 2021 that around 11,500 TARs were supplied for a total of [[Rupee sign|Rs]] 1.60 billion during fiscal year 2020–21.{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210327114640/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/trichy/oft-supplied-over-11k-trichy-assault-rifles-in-this-fiscal/articleshow/81577596.cms|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/trichy/oft-supplied-over-11k-trichy-assault-rifles-in-this-fiscal/articleshow/81577596.cms|title=OFT supplied over 11k Trichy Assault Rifles in this fiscal|work=The Times of India|accessdate=2025-04-16|archivedate=2021-03-27|date=19 March 2021}} In January 2021, the TriCa (Trichy Carbine) Carbine was unveiled. Tests were conducted where 2,000 rounds were fired with no stoppages. That August, OFT announced that the TAR could use the [[ARDE Under Barrel Grenade Launcher]], which was presented by OFT general manager Sanjay Dwivedi.{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430130152/https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Tiruchirapalli/oft-launches-40-x-46-mm-under-barrel-grenade-launcher/article35683036.ece|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Tiruchirapalli/oft-launches-40-x-46-mm-under-barrel-grenade-launcher/article35683036.ece|title=OFT web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406054747/https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1749172|url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1749172|title=Launch of 7.62*39mm web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220416085758/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/trichy/kerala-police-place-order-for-92-trichy-carbine-rifles/articleshow/90831676.cms|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/trichy/kerala-police-place-order-for-92-trichy-carbine-rifles/articleshow/90831676.cms|title=Kerala |url=https://bengali.abplive.com/news/cisf-s-new-rifle-the-trichy-assault-rifle-has-been-manufactured-at-the-ichapur-factory-948995 |title=CISF New Rifle: CISF-এর হাতে নতুন অস্ত্র! মিনিটে ৬০০ গুলি Indigenisation Content is 94%, one of the Highest Among DPSUs, and we Aim for 100%'|date=25 July 2024|publisher=Raksha Anirveda|archivedate=2025-04-16}} In May 2025, it was reported that the Assam Forest Department and the [[Central Bureau of Narcotics]] made orders for the TriCa carbine. ===Development=== Initial versions of the TAR were produced by using [[FN FAL]]-based receivers and were using 7.62x39 mm magazines. In 2012, there were reports that the prototypes jammed during testing due to the rate of fire being 800 rounds per minutes instead of 600 rounds per minute to match with the AK-47. It was initially expected that the rate of fire would be at 650 rounds per minute. The current version of the TAR is based on the AR-M1{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190428150619/https://21stcenturyasianarmsrace.com/2019/01/31/a-new-ak-47-clone-has-come-out-of-india/|url=https://21stcenturyasianarmsrace.com/2019/01/31/a-new-ak-47-clone-has-come-out-of-india/|title=A New AK-47 Clone Has Come Out Of India|date=2019-01-31|accessdate=2025-06-23|archivedate=2019-04-28}} with a machined receiver instead of stamped sheet to ensure the rifle has high accuracy and reliability. The TAR can be outfitted with [[picatinny rail]]s on the upper handguard to attach scopes if requested. ===Combat use=== In July 2021, it was reported that the TARs used by the [[Kerala Police]] are effective in [[Naxalite–Maoist insurgency|Naxalite-Maoist]] [[Counterinsurgency|counterinsurgency operations]].{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210801011950/https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/thiruvananthapuram/2021/Jul/31/govt-gives-nod-to-buy-250-trichy-assault-rifles-2337937.html|url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/thiruvananthapuram/2021/Jul/31/govt-gives-nod-to-buy-250-trichy-assault-rifles-2337937.html|title=Govt gives nod to buy 250 Trichy assault rifles|publisher=The New Indian Express|date=2021-07-31|accessdate=2025-10-30|archivedate=2021-08-01|author=Shan A S}} On August 2025, a TAR was secured from pro-Maoist communist [[People's Liberation Guerrilla Army (India)|Naxalite fighters]] in Chhattisgarh’s [[Narayanpur district]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/cache-of-arms-ammunition-seized-in-5-day-operation-chhattisgarh-police-101756482231132.html|title=Cache of arms, ammunition seized in 5-day operation: Chhattisgarh Police|author=S Kareemuddin|date=2025-08-29|accessdate=2025-09-01|publisher=Hindustan Times}} ==Design== The TAR can fire with single, burst and full automatic mode.{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250417072812/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/trichy/rising-demand-for-trichy-assault-rifle-from-red-corridor-oft-gm/articleshow/63349511.cms|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/trichy/rising-demand-for-trichy-assault-rifle-from-red-corridor-oft-gm/articleshow/63349511.cms|title=Rising demand for Trichy assault rifle from red corridor: OFT GM|work=The Times of India|date=18 March 2018|accessdate=2025-04-17|archivedate=2025-04-17}} OFT reported that the TAR can be adopted with single shot mode only for police forces in cities and urban areas. While it has an effective range of 300 to 350 metres,{{cite web|url=https://aweil.in/download/Annual%20Report%202021-22%20Handbook.pdf?v=1.4|title=ANNUAL REPORT, 2021–2022|publisher=Advanced Weapons and Equipment India|accessdate=2025-04-16|page=11}} the range can be up to 500 metres if the rifle is used in full auto. OFT claimed that the TAR is functionally on par with the AK-47. ===Accessories=== The TAR can be equipped with several [[Grenade launcher|underbarrel grenade launchers]], including the [[ARDE Under Barrel Grenade Launcher|ARDE UBGL]],{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250120213256/https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1741582|url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1741582|title=LAUNCHING OF 40 X 46 mm Under Barrel Grenade Launcher (UBGL) for TAR and AK-47 Rifle|date=2 August 2021|publisher=Press Information Bureau|accessdate=2025-04-16|archivedate=2025-01-20}} the [[GP-25]], the GP-30 and the Arsenal M6 UBGL. The TAR can use bayonets. ===Magazines=== [[Magazine (firearms)|Magazines]] for the TAR are supplied by Nilkamal Limited.{{Cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251031120146/https://www.milipolindia.com/MILIPOL%20SHOW%20GUIDE%202025.pdf|url=https://www.milipolindia.com/MILIPOL%20SHOW%20GUIDE%202025.pdf|title=NILKAMAL LIMITED|publisher=Milipol India|accessdate=2025-10-31|archivedate=2025-10-31|page=51}} Magazines made for [[AK-47]]-based assault rifles can also be used.{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210803064436/https://newsable.asianetnews.com/india-defence/made-in-india-trichy-assault-rifle-gets-a-grenade-launcher-vpn-qx9302|url=https://newsable.asianetnews.com/india-defence/made-in-india-trichy-assault-rifle-gets-a-grenade-launcher-vpn-qx9302|title=Trichy assault rifle now has a grenade launcher option|date=2021-08-03|accessdate=2021-08-03|archivedate=2021-08-03|author=Anish Kumar}} ===Ammunition=== [[7.62×39 mm]] ammunition of all types can be used for the TAR. ==Variants== {{multiple image | align = right | direction = vertical | footer = TAR variants. From top to bottom: TAR side folding stock, TAR down folding stock and TriCa carbine. | image1 = Trichy AR actual model.jpg | width1 = 251 | image2 = TAR folding stock models.jpg | width2 = 251 | image3 = TriCa carbine with folded stock.jpg | width3 = 251 }} ===Trichy assault rifle=== Main variant with a fixed stock. ===Trichy folding stock (side)=== TAR variant with a side folding stock. ===Trichy folding stock (down)=== Unveiled on August 2021, it is a TAR variant with a downfolding stock. It's sometimes referred to as a variant with an underfolding stock. ===Trichy Carbine (TriCa)=== Unveiled on January 2021, the TriCa weights 3.17 kg and is marketed as a compact weapon for vehicle crews, paratroopers and special forces units. The TriCA's firing range is from 150-175 metres. A muzzle device is installed on the barrel to minimize muzzle flash and sound when it's fired. The TriCa is a clone based on the Arsenal AR-M14SF, but the muzzle device is based on the AKS-74U.{{Efn|Mil Mag erroneously referred to it as the '''AKMS-74U'''.{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210809195221/https://milmag.pl/debiut-subkarabinka-trica/|url=https://milmag.pl/debiut-subkarabinka-trica/|title=Debiut subkarabinka TriCaTekst pochodzi z Magazynu Militarnego MILMAG. Przeczytaj więcej|language=Polish|publisher=Mil Mag|accessdate=2025-04-16|archivedate=2021-08-09|date=2021-08-09}}}} It is sometimes known as '''Baby TAR''' or '''TAR-3'''. ==Users== * {{Flag|India}}: ** [[Border Security Force]] ** [[Central Industrial Security Force]] ** [[Central Reserve Police Force]] ** [[Chhattisgarh Police]] ** [[Greater Mumbai Police]] ** [[Indo-Tibetan Border Police]] ** [[Jharkhand Police]] ** [[Kerala Police]] ** [[Madhya Pradesh Police]] ** [[National Security Guard]] ** [[Rajasthan Police]] * Unnamed country: Rajesh Choudhary of AWEIL reported an export order from an unnamed country. ===Non-state actors=== * [[People's Liberation Guerrilla Army (India)]]: At least one Trichy recovered from Naxalite guerrillas. ==Notes== {{notelist}} ==References== {{reflist}} == External links == * {{Commons category-inline|Trichy assault rifle}} {{AK47 derivatives}} [[Category:7.62×39mm assault rifles]] [[Category:Assault rifles of India]] [[Category:Kalashnikov derivatives]] [[Category:Weapons and ammunition introduced in 2017]]
